Paradoxically, the Jerusalem artichoke is neither an artichoke nor from Jerusalem.
This vegetable is the thick, brown-skinned root of a variety of sunflower. The
mature tubers or roots, most of which are 3 to 4 inches long and about half as
thick, resemble small, lumpy Irish potatoes. The white flesh of the Jerusalem 
artichoke is usually described 
as nutty, sweet, 
and crunchy.
